entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Flavius Rufinus was a 4th-century Eastern Roman statesman of Aquitanian extraction who served as Praetorian prefect of the East for the emperor Theodosius I, as well as for his son Arcadius, under whom Rufinus exercised significant influence in the state affairs.

Rufinus was instrumental in shaping the Eastern Roman Empire's relations with the Gothic kingdoms and the Huns, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the late Roman world.

His tenure also saw the rise of Christianity as the official state religion, with Rufinus playing a key role in promoting the faith among the Roman elite and beyond.

The legacy of Rufinus can be seen in the continued influence of the Eastern Roman Empire on the development of Byzantine society and culture, as well as in the ongoing debates among historians about the role of Christianity in the Roman Empire's decline and fall.

"The world is not a stage, but a tapestry." - Rufinus, as quoted in the letters of his contemporary, St. Jerome.
